name: obsidian-router
description: Slash commands, skills, sub-agents, and hooks for the obsidian-mcp-router multi-vault MCP server — and, since v0.56.0, the MCP server itself: installing the plugin installs the server, and one update refreshes server + commands + skills + hooks together. 54 /obsidian-router:* commands across four layers: (1) 18 wrappers for the router's MCP primitives (discover/read/write/manage/template/convert); (2) 4 router-state commands (lock / unlock for single-vault isolation, auto-mode for the wiki auto-enrichment mode, force-new-port-start to move the allocation base for FUTURE vaults); (3) 7 conversational helpers (meta-setup, meta-attach-vault, meta-status, meta-sync-template, meta-audit-bridge-readiness, conventions, sync-from-github); (4) a 22-command Karpathy-style LLM-wiki workflow (wiki, wiki-ingest, wiki-query, wiki-lint, wiki-fold, wiki-graph, wiki-tour, wiki-export, okf-export, okf-check, okf-projections, save, decision-consolidate, autoresearch, canvas, defuddle, obsidian-bases, ...). Plus 49 skills (incl. the reference-only obsidian-markdown) and 2 parallel sub-agents. Three hooks are active on install (hot-cache-load, workspace-briefing, decisions-recall — read-only on vaults, each with an env opt-out; each leaves a heartbeat file beside the router config so list_vaults can say whether the session's hooks ran); the other 8 stay opt-in via setup-vault.mjs --install-hooks. Since v0.101.0 the plugin also loads a vault panel (a function-hooks module): a Vaults pane and a /vaults command showing the workspace's primary vault, its secondaries with their write tier, and the vaults that can be added — changed only on a click, through the router's own tools (opt-out OBSIDIAN_ROUTER_NO_VAULT_PANEL).
